source_text:
Fragmentum in librum Baruch
FRAGMENTA EX CATENIS IN LIBRUM BARUCH
Ὅτι σὺ καθήμενος εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα. Ἀεὶ γὰρ καὶ ἐν παντὶ χρόνῳ φθαρτή ἐστιν ἡ
πεποιημένη φύσις, καὶ τῶν γεννητῶν ἐν τούτοις τὸ μέτρον. Κάθηται δὲ ἡ πάντων
τεχνῖτις καὶ δημιουργὸς σοφία, τουτέστιν ἀκλόνητον ἔχει τὴν ἐν ταυτότητι
διαμονήν. Καὶ πάλιν· Ἡμῶν γὰρ κάθισις ἐν τούτοις τὸ ἀκράδαντόν τε καὶ ἱδρυμένον
τῆς ὑπάρξεως, καὶ διαμονῆς τῆς ἀνωτάτω πασῶν οὐσίας ὑποδηλοῖ· τὸ δὲ, ἡμᾶς
pass_a_gloss: Fragment on the book of Baruch. Fragments from the catenae on the book of Baruch. Because you [are] seated unto the age. For always and in every time the made nature is perishable, and of the generated ones the measure [is] in these. But the craftswoman and demiurge of all things, Wisdom, sits — that is, she has unshaken the continuance in sameness. And again: For our sitting in these shows both the unshakeable and the established of existence, and of continuance of the highest of all substances; but [as for] us…
pass_b_english: Baruch says you are seated unto the age. Made nature is always perishable in every time, and generated things have their measure in that frailty. But Wisdom, craftswoman and maker of all, sits — that is, she keeps unshaken continuance in sameness. Again: our sitting shows the unshakeable, established character of existence and of the continuance of the highest of all substances; but as for us…
